title: Opera browser profile
whyItMatters: The Opera profile holds history, sessions, bookmarks and saved logins. Anyone who takes the disk can see what was browsed and which sites kept the user signed in.
source: Opera on Linux keeps its user data root in ~/.config/opera (opera://about shows the exact profile and cache paths): https://filepathgeek.com/posts/opera-browser-profile-location
notes: Opera One builds put the profile in a Default subfolder; older builds wrote Preferences directly into ~/.config/opera, which this glob does not match. Opera GX uses ~/.config/opera-gx; Beta and Developer builds have their own folders.

cleanup.exportFirst: In Opera, save your bookmarks with the bookmark manager's export option and copy the Login Data file from the folder named in the plan.
cleanup.signOut: In Opera, sign out of your Opera account in the browser settings, so the account keeps the synced data and this computer stops using it.
steps: Uninstall Opera from the App Center, or from the Snap or Flatpak tool if you installed it that way.
Move the folder named in the plan to the Trash and empty the Trash.
cleanup.risk: Removes every Opera profile on this computer: history, bookmarks, saved passwords, cookies, extensions and open tabs.
cleanup.source: Opera Help, Crashes and issues - back up your Opera files: https://help.opera.com/en/latest/crashes-and-issues/
